# Notes on the 2026-09-01 record

**This file is hand-written.** Everything else in this directory is generated by
`tools/gsv-fov-probe/analyze.mjs --copy-recorded` (`results.json`, `report.md`, `manifest-extract.json`, and
the same three under `quarterly/`). Don't edit those by hand — re-run the analyzer instead.

## Cross-channel comparison: weekly vs quarterly

Two runs on the same day against the same scenes:

| | run | Maps version | scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| weekly (primary) | `2026-09-01T02-19-24-024Z` | `3.66.2d` | full sweep, 10 containers × 4 scenes × zooms 1–3 |
| quarterly (stability check) | `2026-09-01T18-31-57-133Z` | `3.65.12f` | `control-720x480` + `xwide-2400x480` only |

Over the **32 cells the two runs share**, every median focal length is **bit-identical** — `fCss` matches to
full precision in all 32, so `hFov` and `vFov` do too (max difference 0.0000°). Both runs return
`width-pinned-vfov-clamped` with the same floor (14.974°); the quarterly run's container subset never reaches
the ceiling, so it estimates no ceiling. The two Maps channels render the same projection.

Derivation, from the two committed `results.json` files (no raw run data needed):

```bash
node -e "
const w = require('./tools/gsv-fov-probe/recorded/2026-09-01/results.json');
const q = require('./tools/gsv-fov-probe/recorded/2026-09-01/quarterly/results.json');
const key = (c) => [c.panoName, c.containerName, c.zoom, c.kind].join('|');
const wm = new Map(w.cells.map((c) => [key(c), c]));
const shared = q.cells.filter((c) => wm.has(key(c)));
const identical = shared.filter((c) => c.fCss === wm.get(key(c)).fCss);
console.log(shared.length, identical.length);
"
```
